blindComparison: A stranger shown phone-sun-r15v1.png beside a Sekiro dusk gate or a Tsushima torii approach picks the reference, and the reason is the air. In our frame the sun disc sits directly behind a torii post, a shimenawa, four shide streamers and two paper lanterns - the textbook occluder stack - and produces no shafts at all, only a smooth milky wash. Measured: along an arc of radius 0.10W around the disc in `sun` the sky reads 215,223,222,204,221,222,207,226,234,234,234,233,221 - a single smooth hump with no angular structure; in `valley` the band under the sun reads 200,204,207,212,219,221,220,218,216,221,215,208, same. So the atmosphere reads as flat fog rather than light with direction, and the sky above it is an achromatic grey card (hero sun-side sky saturation 0.018-0.062 across the whole column). The reference wins because its low sun cuts hard volumetric bars through the same geometry and its sky carries a real warm-to-cool gradient - that is what tells the eye the sun is low, and ours never says it.
notesOnApparatus: All findings were cropped and probed at native 2532x1170 before filing. Two candidate findings were killed by that check and are recorded here so nobody re-files them: (1) an apparent field of RGB confetti in dark ground - it was my own decoder reading a 3-channel PNG with a stride of 4; corrected, per-pixel high-pass SD in flat sky is 0.22-0.40, i.e. no chroma noise. (2) 'no cast shadows on the plaza' - FALSE. phone-sun-r15v1.png crop 0.32,0.72,0.30,0.28 shows the near torii post and a stone lantern throwing long, correctly-directed shadows across the flagstone, and the fence in `valley` throws clean per-picket shadows on the terrace. Shadows work. I also nearly filed 'lantern ground-spill discs read as hard-edged pale coasters' - zoomed 3x at 0.435,0.79,0.08,0.10 in `wide` they are soft warm pools and are fine. Vermilion was also checked and is correct: torii posts measure RGB [170.6,49.7,23.7] and [142.7,42.0,19.7], saturation 0.87, close to the contract's #c8321e; earlier-looking 'washed pink' readings were edge contamination from the sky. Sky banding was checked with a 16x contrast stretch and is dithered cleanly - not a finding.

findings.problem: There are no volumetric god-ray shafts anywhere in the review set, including in the two shots framed specifically to produce them. In phone-sun-r15v1.png the sun disc sits at (1525,532) with a torii post, the shimenawa, four shide paper streamers and two chochin hanging directly across it (see crop 0.36,0.08,0.34,0.48) and the sky behind them is a perfectly smooth radial gradient - no bright wedges through the gaps, no dark wedges behind the occluders. Sampling an arc of radius 0.10*width centred on the disc, sky-only sector 100deg to 200deg, mean luma over a 13x13 box reads: 215.2, 222.6, 222.3, 204.4, 221.4, 222.4, 207.3, 226.0, 234.4, 234.5, 234.4, 233.2, 221.5 - one smooth hump, no angular modulation. In phone-valley-r15v1.png, where isolated bamboo culms stand between the camera and the sun, a horizontal sky band at y=0.13 sampled in twelve 0.03x0.04 boxes from x=0.16 to x=0.60 reads p50 luma 200,204,207,212,219,221,220,218,216,221,215,208 - again a single unimodal radial falloff, adjacent-sample delta never exceeding 6 code values. What is present is bloom around bright sources, not scattering along the light's path.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE section 5 non-negotiable #4 is 'volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo'. It is the feature that turns a low sun into a lighting event rather than a bright spot, and it is the single most recognisable thing about a Sekiro or Tsushima dusk frame. Without it the haze reads as uniform fog: the air has brightness but no direction, so the sun stops being a light source in the scene and becomes a sticker on the sky.
findings.fix: Produce visible radial shafts anchored on the sun, occluded by scene depth. Acceptance, both measurable with tools/probe.mjs on a re-shot phone review set: (a) in `sun`, on the arc of radius 0.10*width around the sun centre (0.602,0.455), sector 100deg-200deg sampled at 25 points, the profile must show at least 3 local minima each at least 15 code values below the mean of their two neighbours, aligned with the shide/shimenawa silhouettes; (b) in `valley`, the horizontal band y=0.13, x=0.16..0.60 sampled in twelve 0.03x0.04 boxes must show at least 3 local maxima separated by dips of at least 12 code values, instead of the current monotone-in-from-both-sides hump. Do not chase this with `detail` (mean |Laplacian|) - a 1-pixel Laplacian cannot see a 60px-period shaft and will report a smooth gradient as higher-detail than banding. Use the arc/band profiles above. Keep the peak sky luma near the disc at or below its current 234 so the shafts are produced by removing light in the shadowed wedges, not by adding more white.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING - prove or disprove before acting: the pass may be running but with its radial weight so low that the result is indistinguishable from the bloom halo, or the occluder buffer may be receiving a cleared/near-uniform input so every sample along the ray returns the same value and the accumulation flattens to a radial falloff. The r15 note that a previous round raised the god-ray weight 4-6x and made the frame worse suggests weight alone is not the lever; check first whether the occlusion input actually varies across the shide streamers before touching any gain.

findings.problem: The sky dome is an achromatic grey card with almost no gradient, in a set whose entire premise is magic hour. In phone-hero-r15v1.png, sampling the sun-side sky column at x=0.905 in 0.06x0.03 boxes from the top of frame down to the horizon (y = 0.02, 0.08, 0.14, 0.20, 0.26, 0.32) gives p50 luma 165.7, 162.6, 169.7, 176.8, 178.9, 179.8 - a 17 code-value swing over the whole sky - at saturations of 0.039, 0.018, 0.031, 0.047, 0.045, 0.062. That is neutral grey, not sky. Within a single 506x152 box at 0.75,0.01 the total p1-to-p99 luma range is 158.6 to 173.8, i.e. 15 code values; the cloud forms that exist are a 6%-contrast modulation and are invisible at normal viewing. phone-wide-r15v1.png sky at 0.86,0.03 measures RGB [144.4,158.8,160.7], saturation 0.101, p1-p99 spread 8.5. phone-torii-r15v1.png is the best of the three and still only moves p50 luma 125 to 152 from top of frame to horizon, with horizon RGB [152.9,136.8,129.3] - barely warm. Nowhere in the set does the sky within 45 degrees of the sun go amber, rose or orange.
findings.why: This is priority items 1 and 3 on the critic list at once - tonal range and colour - and it poisons everything below it. The sky is 25-35% of three of the five frames and it is also the brightest thing in every one of them, so the eye reads it first and takes its cue from it: a flat grey ceiling says 'overcast late afternoon'. The reported sun is (1.0, 0.412, 0.134) at 13 degrees elevation, which physically cannot coexist with a saturation-0.02 sky; the frame is contradicting its own key light. It also causes the second-order read that the ground looks wrong: key-lit plaza in `torii` sits at p50 luma 46-62 while the grey sky sits at 147-158, so the world looks like it is lit from above by a softbox instead of raked by a low sun.
findings.fix: Give the dome a real magic-hour gradient with chroma. Acceptance, all on a re-shot phone set with tools/probe.mjs: (a) in `hero`, the sun-side sky column at x=0.905 must move at least 60 code values in p50 luma between y=0.02 and y=0.32 (currently 17); (b) at least two of those six boxes, the ones nearest the horizon, must reach saturation >= 0.25 with R > G > B (currently max saturation anywhere in that column is 0.062 and R < G at the top); (c) in `wide`, the sky box at 0.86,0.03 must reach saturation >= 0.20 (currently 0.101); (d) the zenith must stay cool - keep B > R at y=0.02 in `torii` (currently correct at [104.7,129.2,144.6]) so the frame gains a warm-horizon-to-cool-zenith axis rather than just getting more orange overall. Do not solve this by raising exposure: pctAbove240 must stay below 0.5% in every shot (currently 0.005-0.304%).
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING: the horizon-warmth term may be keyed off the sun's screen position rather than its world direction, so it only appears in the two shots that point at the sun (`sun` and `valley` do carry warm sky, saturation 0.10-0.30 near the disc) and vanishes in the three that do not. Check whether the same dome shader produces a warm horizon band when the camera faces 180 degrees away from the sun before changing any colour constants.

findings.problem: The forested hillside that fills the left third of the establishing shot is built from flat-topped vertical rectangles. Zoom 3x on region 0.04,0.235,0.10,0.09 (source pixels 101,275, 253x105): every 'tree' is a rectangle with hard vertical left and right edges and a perfectly flat horizontal top, filled with mottled green. They vary only in width and height - there is no canopy shape, no taper, no branch silhouette, no crown. You can count them individually at (101+100,275+130), (+200,+155), (+270,+165), (+350,+190), (+440,+175), (+500,+150), (+610,+155), (+700,+80). The band covers roughly x 0.02-0.35, y 0.22-0.48 of the frame - about a quarter of the image area - and measures RGB [95.1,97.0,86.6], saturation 0.126, p50 luma 95.8. The same rectangles appear behind the haiden in `hero` at 0.00,0.30,0.28,0.40. Additionally, no tree in the band occludes or shadows any other, so the whole mass sits at one uniform value with no depth.
findings.why: Critic priority 6, silhouette. Squint at the contact sheet and the hillside resolves into a green bar chart - it is the single most obviously synthetic element in the set and it is in the establishing frame, the one that sells the place. Tsushima's mid-distance forests read as forests at thumbnail size specifically because the crown silhouette is irregular and the canopy self-occludes into light and dark clumps. Ours reads as a texture applied to a row of posts.
findings.fix: Break the flat rectangular tops and give the band internal value structure. Acceptance on a re-shot `wide`: (a) crop 0.04,0.235,0.10,0.09 at 3x must show no straight horizontal top edge longer than 8 source pixels on any tree - crowns must be irregular; (b) the band region 0.05,0.28,0.10,0.10 must reach a p1-to-p99 luma spread of at least 70 (currently 36.7, i.e. 79.1 to 115.8) from tree-to-tree lighting and self-occlusion, not from adding noise to the texture; (c) mean luma of the band must stay within +/-10 of its current 95.8 so this does not turn into a brightness change. Note this band is `foliage/far-cover`, 5134 instances at 20536 triangles in the r15v1 draw list - there is headroom in the budget (115 of 140 draw calls, 735k of 900k triangles) for a slightly richer card silhouette, but a cheaper fix is a crown-shaped alpha and per-instance vertical scatter.

findings.problem: A large flat-black patch lies on the plaza floor with no ambient floor and no stone texture inside it. Connected-component scan of phone-hero-r15v1.png for luma < 10 below y=0.6 finds a 10,493-pixel region with bounding box (1283,973) to (1494,1065), fill factor 0.53 - a lobed, scalloped outline made of overlapping circles, hard-edged, sitting immediately left of a stone lantern base. Interior measures RGB [5.7,4.7,5.6], p50 luma 3.1, probe `detail` 2.98. The flagstone 30 px directly above it (box 1317,945 114x16) is already in cool sky-lit shadow and measures RGB [29.3,33.1,39.3], p50 luma 32.6, `detail` 5.95 - correctly cool with B > R and with the stone texture still resolvable. So this patch is ten times darker than the properly-shaded stone touching it, and the flagstone pattern that runs right up to its rim disappears inside. The boundary steps from luma ~33 to luma ~3 within about 3 pixels, with no penumbra. Its outline matches no object in the scene: the stone lantern beside it is a slender shaft with a flared roof, not a chain of discs. See crop 0.44,0.79,0.20,0.19 at 2x.
findings.why: It reads as a hole in the ground, or a PS2-era blob-shadow decal - the one thing a shipped title never has. It is 3-5 metres from camera in the hero framing, dead centre-bottom where the eye lands, and it undoes the credibility of an otherwise convincing plaza. It is also a shading contradiction the viewer can feel without naming: the frame proves 30 px away that it knows how to render a cool sky-lit shadow at luma 33, and then puts pure black next to it.
findings.fix: No connected region of the plaza floor may sit below luma 10 for more than 400 pixels. Specifically the region bounded by (1283,973)-(1494,1065) in a re-shot `hero` must land in the same tonal family as the shaded flagstone immediately above it: mean RGB approximately [29,33,39] with B > R, p50 luma >= 25, and probe `detail` >= 5.0 over box 0.520,0.850,0.045,0.045 so the flagstone texture is still readable inside it. Re-run the connected-component check (threshold luma < 10, lower 40% of frame) and confirm the 10,493-pixel component is gone. Do not fix this by lifting global ambient - the surrounding shadow tone at [29,33,39] is already correct and must not move by more than 5 code values.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING - disprove before acting: this may not be a CSM shadow at all. Three things argue against it: the equivalent stone lanterns in `torii` (crop 0.55,0.62,0.42,0.38) have no such patch beside them; the outline is a chain of overlapping discs rather than any object's silhouette; and cast shadows demonstrably work elsewhere in this same build (`sun` crop 0.32,0.72,0.30,0.28 shows a long correctly-directed post shadow, `valley` shows per-picket fence shadows on the terrace). A ground-plane quad associated with the stone lanterns is worth ruling out before any cascade or bias parameter is touched. The r15v1 report lists `level/lantern-pool:__glowPool`, 24 instances, additive blending, opacity 0.38 - if that geometry is involved the owner is src/world/Props.js or src/world/Level.js, not this file, and that should be reported back rather than worked around.

findings.problem: The paving material loses its joint network wherever the light is not raking, so at close range the ground becomes a jointless mottle. In phone-valley-r15v1.png the stone terrace 2-4 m from camera (crop 0.45,0.48,0.30,0.35) is a broad soft plane whose only structure is a handful of thin dark crack lines forming one large X across a ~5 m span; between them the surface is a uniform fine speckle with no paving cells, no per-stone value difference, no chipped or rounded edges, no debris or moss in the joints, and a broad soft specular sheen that reads as damp plastic sheeting rather than wet stone. In phone-hero-r15v1.png the plaza 3-5 m from camera (crop 0.44,0.79,0.20,0.19 at 2x) is an amorphous mottle of soft irregular patches with no joint network at all. Compare the same material under raking light in phone-sun-r15v1.png (crop 0.06,0.82,0.16,0.14): there the polygonal paving cells and their joints read clearly. Same surface, three distances, and the structure only survives where N.L is high.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE section 5 non-negotiable #9 - no untextured flat-colour surfaces, everything has grain. There is grain here, but at the wrong scale: fine speckle and nothing at the 30-60 cm paving pitch the eye needs to believe stones were laid. Critic priority 7, material response. The nearest surface in the frame is the one the player judges the whole renderer by, and at 2 m a stone terrace that shows no individual stones reads as a painted plane.
findings.fix: Make the paving joints survive at low N.L. Acceptance on a re-shot phone set: in `valley` crop 0.45,0.48,0.30,0.35 and `hero` crop 0.44,0.79,0.20,0.19, the ground must resolve a joint network with a mean cell spacing of 20-45 screen pixels; joints must sit at least 20 code values below the adjacent stone face; and adjacent stone faces must differ from each other by at least 12 code values in mean luma so the surface reads as laid units rather than one poured slab. Verify by eye on a 2x nearest-neighbour zoom of both crops, and hold the region mean luma within +/-8 of its current value (valley terrace 79.7, hero plaza 35.0) so this is a structure change and not a brightness change.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING - disprove before acting: the joints may exist only in the normal map with no albedo or AO contribution, which would explain exactly why they appear under the raking light of `sun` and vanish in the flatter light of `hero` and the `valley` terrace. Sample the albedo and AO channels of the paving texture at a joint texel and at a face texel before changing any noise parameters; if they are identical, the fix is to write the joint into albedo/AO, not to increase normal strength.

findings.problem: The sakura canopy has no petal, cluster or branch structure at any distance. At 1:1 in phone-hero-r15v1.png (crop 0.13,0.10,0.10,0.13, source 329,117, 253x152) the blossom mass resolves into amorphous purple-brown and salmon smears - there is no petal silhouette, no cluster edge, and no readable branch running through the crown; the few thin dark lines present read as scratches, not limbs. The full canopy (crop 0.04,0.02,0.30,0.38) is two flat colour populations, a salmon key-lit one and a muddy grey-violet shaded one, with the boundary between them scattered as noise rather than following any form. Region 0.10,0.10,0.14,0.16 measures mean RGB [129.1,85.5,98.2], saturation 0.344, p50 luma 89.2. At mid distance in phone-torii-r15v1.png (behind the gate at roughly 0.24-0.36, 0.37-0.60) it is a pale lavender cloud, and in phone-wide-r15v1.png it is a flat pink cotton-wool heart at (830,400) with zero internal structure. The canopy is roughly 12% of the `hero` frame and is the brightest, most saturated object in it, so it is the first thing the eye goes to.
findings.why: Critic priority 6 and 7. A cherry tree is the most photographed object in this entire genre and every viewer has a reference for it. Tsushima's blossom canopies read because they have three legible scales - petal, cluster, crown - plus dark structural branches visible through the mass and warm translucency where the low sun passes through the petals. Ours has one scale, mush, and no light passing through it. Being the eye's first stop in the hero frame makes it the costliest single object in the set.
findings.fix: Give the canopy legible cluster structure and let the branches read. Acceptance on a re-shot `hero`: (a) in a 3x nearest-neighbour zoom of crop 0.13,0.10,0.10,0.13, discrete blossom clusters must be countable - at least 12 separable cluster silhouettes in that 253x152 source region, each with a resolvable edge against its neighbour; (b) at least two dark branch runs at least 60 source pixels long must be visible passing through the crown interior; (c) the region 0.10,0.10,0.14,0.16 must reach a p1-to-p99 luma spread of at least 150 (currently 128.6) with the sun-facing clusters carrying warm translucency - R > G > B and R at least 40 above B on the lit population; (d) keep mean luma within +/-10 of the current 89.2 p50 so this is a structure and colour-separation change, not a brightening. If the crown is drawn as cards, per-card alpha with a cluster silhouette plus depth-sorted overlap will do more than any shading change.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING: the r15v1 draw list names this geometry `level/level:static:0,0:__blossom`, which suggests it is merged by src/world/Level.js even if the cards are authored here. If Foliage.js does not own the blossom cards, say so and hand the routing back rather than duplicating a tree implementation - ARCHITECTURE section 8 puts trees under this file, so confirm which is true before either owner edits.

findings.problem: The shot briefed as 'bamboo sea from the overlook' shows a flat plain at eye level with no overlook, no valley and no bamboo sea. In phone-valley-r15v1.png the ground runs unbroken from the bottom of the frame up to a single treeline at y=0.33 with no drop-off edge, no valley floor below the camera, no receding ridge layers and no mist band separating any distance planes - the only depth cue is a uniform warm haze. The bamboo that is present is about 20 isolated spindly culms scattered across the frame (x 1050 to 1900, tops around y=0.02-0.10) standing in front of a green wall of cards; it reads as a handful of poles, not a sea. WORLD puts the water level 30 m below the plateau and the valley on azimuth 135, so a drop exists in the world and this pose is not looking down it.
findings.why: Critic priority 4 and 5, composition and aerial perspective. This is the shot that is supposed to deliver the single most evocative line in the art direction - a mountain shrine above a bamboo sea at magic hour, mist in the valley - and it delivers a field. A flat plain at eye level has one distance plane, so the atmospheric haze has nothing to grade between and reads as a fog filter rather than depth. It is also the frame where god rays would have the most to work with, and a valley full of mist is the standard way that reads.
findings.fix: Re-pose the `valley` shot so the camera actually stands above the drop and looks down it. Acceptance on a re-shot `valley`: (a) a visible drop edge - a horizontal break beyond which no ground is visible for at least 40 px of screen height - must appear within the lower half of the frame; (b) at least three distinguishable distance planes must be present between that edge and the horizon, each separated from the next by at least 12 code values of mean luma (measure with 0.10x0.03 probe boxes stacked vertically at x=0.5); (c) the far horizon line must sit at or above y=0.30 with the intervening terrain reading as lower than the camera. Aim the pose along WORLD.VALLEY_AZIMUTH = 135 from the plateau edge. If, after re-aiming, there is genuinely no 30 m drop in the terrain within the shot's view distance, report that back rather than re-framing around it - that would make the owner src/world/Terrain.js, not this file.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING: the pose may be sited inside PLATEAU_RADIUS (78 m) rather than out at the plateau lip, so the camera is standing on the flattened shrine floor with the drop still beyond the visible horizon. Check the shot's XZ distance from PLATEAU_CENTER against 78+34 m before assuming the terrain lacks a valley.

findings.problem: The right 45% of the establishing frame is undressed ground. Region x 0.55-1.0, y 0.52-0.85 of phone-wide-r15v1.png (see crop 0.55,0.55,0.32,0.42) is one uniform surface - measured at 0.70,0.62,0.12,0.10: mean RGB [46.9,48.9,51.6], saturation 0.184, p50 luma 49.4 - stippled at constant density with identically sized, identically oriented dark vegetation marks running unchanged all the way to the horizon. In that whole area there is a bridge, two fence runs, and nothing else: no path, no stone edging, no worn track, no rock, no fallen timber, no rubbish, no asymmetry, no landmark. The frame's entire subject is packed into the left third and the rest is filler.
findings.why: Critic priority 8, density and dressing, and priority 4, composition. Real places have clutter, wear and asymmetry, and the uniform-density scatter is the giveaway that this was generated rather than placed - the eye reads a constant stipple as a texture, not a landscape. It is also why this frame's histogram is the flattest of the set (p1 17, p10 33, p50 89, p99 196, only 0.554% of pixels below luma 16): nearly half the image is one tone with nothing in it to make a shadow or a highlight.
findings.fix: Dress the right half of the plateau. Acceptance on a re-shot `wide`: (a) at least three distinct pieces of placed dressing must be readable in region x 0.55-1.0, y 0.52-0.85 at thumbnail size - candidates that fit the setting are a stacked-stone retaining edge, a woodpile or stacked timber, a small stone jizo cluster, sake cask stacks, a worn earth track branching off the sando; (b) the ground in that region must stop being one tone - measured over the same 0.70,0.62,0.12,0.10 box, the p1-to-p99 luma spread must exceed 100 (currently 57.7) from placed objects and their shadows, not from raising contrast; (c) the whole-frame pctBelow16 must rise above 2.5% (currently 0.554%) as a consequence of real dark objects entering the right half. Keep the draw budget in mind: r15v1 sits at 115 of 140 calls and 784k of 900k triangles in this shot, so instance or merge whatever is added.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING: the uniform-density vegetation stipple in this region is a scatter characteristic and may belong to src/render/Foliage.js rather than to placed dressing. If clustering the scatter is the right lever, hand that half back to Foliage rather than placing props to hide it.

findings.problem: The sun disc renders as a neutral clipped white circle. In phone-sun-r15v1.png the disc at box 0.594,0.440,0.018,0.035 measures RGB [254.4,254.4,251.6], saturation 0.011, p50 luma 254.6; the sky 60 px away at 0.625,0.445 measures [236.7,232.5,213.2], saturation 0.099. In phone-valley-r15v1.png the disc at 0.355,0.015,0.035,0.055 measures saturation 0.039 with p50 luma 241.4. The reported sun colour for this time of day is (1.0, 0.412, 0.134). So the disc is less saturated than the sky it sits in, and reads as a small white ball - closer to a moon or a blown highlight than to a low sun.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE section 5 non-negotiable #1 asks for a real sun disc. At 13 degrees elevation the disc is seen through the longest atmospheric path of the day and is the warmest thing in the frame; a neutral-white one contradicts the whole time-of-day premise at the exact point the eye is drawn to.
findings.fix: The disc must be warmer than the sky immediately around it. Acceptance on a re-shot `sun`: box 0.594,0.440,0.018,0.035 must measure saturation >= 0.18 with R > G > B, and its R-minus-B must exceed that of the sky box at 0.625,0.445 by at least 15. Keep p50 luma of the disc at or above 235 so it still reads as the brightest thing in frame, and keep whole-frame pctAbove240 below 0.5% (currently 0.274%). A wider, warmer scattering halo around the disc is the cheap way to get both this and the sky-gradient finding at once.

findings.problem: Film grain is effectively absent. Measuring per-pixel high-pass residual (pixel minus its 3x3 mean) in flat sky regions where nothing else varies: phone-hero-r15v1.png at 0.70,0.02,0.14,0.05 gives per-channel SD 0.23 / 0.22 / 0.23; phone-wide-r15v1.png at 0.86,0.03 gives 0.25 / 0.26 / 0.27; phone-sun-r15v1.png at 0.03,0.03 gives 0.26 / 0.23 / 0.23; phone-torii-r15v1.png at 0.05,0.02 gives 0.40 / 0.40 / 0.40. A quarter of a code value is below the visible threshold on any display.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE section 5 non-negotiable #7 asks for subtle grain, and critic priority 9. Grain is what stops large smooth areas - and this set has very large smooth areas, given the flat sky - from reading as vector art. It is also the cheapest way to hide the residual quantisation in a 15-code-value sky gradient. Note the sky is currently dithered cleanly (checked at 16x contrast stretch, no contour steps), so this is about surface character, not banding.
findings.fix: Raise grain to a visible but subtle level. Acceptance: per-channel high-pass SD measured in the four flat-sky boxes above must land between 1.2 and 2.5 code values (currently 0.22-0.40), equal across R/G/B so it stays luminance grain rather than chroma noise. Confirm it does not leak into the shadows as noise: the same measurement in `hero` box 0.10,0.60,0.08,0.06 must not exceed 4.0 (currently 3.65 from real texture).

findings.problem: No falling sakura, no drifting embers and no discrete mist layer appear in any of the five frames. Inspected at native resolution directly beneath the blossom tree in phone-hero-r15v1.png (crop 0.08,0.42,0.24,0.30) - the region where petals would be densest against a dark plaza - there are none. None appear against the dark left-hand pavilions, against the sky in `wide`, or against the backlit haze in `valley` or `sun`. The only atmospheric element anywhere in the set is a uniform distance haze; there is no mist bank sitting in a hollow, no layered fog ribbon, nothing with an edge.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE section 5 names 'mist in the valley' and 'falling sakura and drifting embers' as the setting, and they are the cheapest way to give a still frame life and to break up large flat areas. In the reference titles the drifting particulate is a signature, not a garnish - it is a large part of why a Tsushima still does not look like a still.
